import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Convert the sex column to a categorical variable
df['Sex of respondent, 1979'] = df['Sex of respondent, 1979'].astype('category')

# Create a boxplot to visualize the relationship between gender and highest grade completed
sns.boxplot(x='Sex of respondent, 1979', y='Highest grade completed, 1979', data=df)
plt.title('Relationship between Gender and Highest Grade Completed')
plt.xlabel('Gender')
plt.ylabel('Highest Grade Completed')
plt.show()

from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

# Filter the data by gender
male_data = df[df['Sex of respondent, 1979'] == 1]['Highest grade completed, 1979']
female_data = df[df['Sex of respondent, 1979'] == 2]['Highest grade completed, 1979']

# Perform a t-test to compare the means of the two groups
t_statistic, p_value = ttest_ind(male_data, female_data)
t_statistic, p_value

# Check for missing values in the relevant columns
missing_values = df[['Sex of respondent, 1979', 'Highest grade completed, 1979']].isnull().sum()
missing_values
